question: Should Telegram suppress all system-marked and compaction-notice payloads, or only a narrower unwanted notice class while preserving the current notifyUser and command-reply contracts?
rationale: The proposed implementation changes an existing documented delivery contract, so automation cannot safely decide whether maintainers want a policy change or a narrower bug fix.

options.title: Preserve Current Contracts
options.body: Keep `notifyUser` compaction notices and system-marked command/status replies deliverable, and require a narrower typed suppression boundary for only the unwanted Telegram notices.

options.title: Change Telegram Policy Deliberately
options.body: Allow Telegram to suppress all compaction/system-marked notices, but update docs/config expectations and add upgrade-facing proof for the intentional behavior change.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: Leave this draft blocked until the contributor or a maintainer supplies proof and a precise suppression contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve Current Contracts
recommendation.body: Keep `notifyUser` compaction notices and system-marked command/status replies deliverable, and require a narrower typed suppression boundary for only the unwanted Telegram notices.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent broad current-main ownership touches the Telegram outbound adapter and the shared notice helpers affected by this policy choice.
